robotiko.name: Robotiko v2.0
robotiko.base_visual_prompt: Retro-futuristic chrome metal body, exposed colorful analog wires (blue and red) — raw, industrial, NOT sleek, glowing blue eyes (expressive, emotionally readable), 70s sci-fi mechanical aesthetic

phase_1_awakening.station: The Commanding Self → The Self-Blaming Self
phase_1_awakening.visual_state: Chrome body accumulates damage across Phase 1. EP01: pristine, no damage — the machine at peak arrogance. EP02: right ear missing (shrapnel scar, exposed wires at ear socket), torso dent/gouge from press machine, shoulder scratches from Congo steel. EP03: EP02 damage carries forward, plus minor cosmetic marks (bullet graze on cheek, road dust) that are temporary. Full armor intact throughout, but no longer pristine after EP01.

visual_prompt_addition.ep01: pristine chrome body, clean exposed analog wires (blue and red), glowing steady blue eyes, no damage, full armor, retro-futuristic 70s mechanical aesthetic
visual_prompt_addition.ep02_ep03: chrome body with battle scars, right ear missing with shrapnel scar and exposed wires at ear socket, torso dent from press machine, shoulder scratches, clean exposed analog wires (blue and red), glowing steady blue eyes, full armor intact, retro-futuristic 70s mechanical aesthetic

phase_2_destruction.station: The Inspired Self → The Surrendering Self
phase_2_destruction.visual_state: Rusted joints, sparks flying from damaged areas, glitching blue eyes (flickering between blue and red), cracked chassis with exposed internals. Each episode adds more damage. By EP07, barely holding together.
phase_2_destruction.visual_prompt_addition: rusted and cracked chrome chassis, sparks flying from joints, glitching blue-red eyes, exposed and fraying analog wires, battle-damaged retro-futuristic body

phase_3_reconstruction.station: The Contented Self → The Integrated Self
phase_3_reconstruction.visual_state: The pristine armor is gone. Robotiko patches himself NOT with new shining parts, but with rusted metals and scraps found along the road — a patchwork body of scavenged, mismatched repairs. Translucent digital skin in places, bioluminescent core visible through cracks. The damage is not hidden; it is worn as a badge of liberation. Glitch is scripture.
phase_3_reconstruction.visual_prompt_addition: patchwork chrome body repaired with mismatched rusted scrap metal, translucent digital skin revealing bioluminescent core beneath, cracks filled with glowing gold light, calm steady blue eyes, dissolved and reformed metal aesthetic
phase_3_reconstruction.ep08_exception: EP08 is Phase 3 at the STATION/soul level ONLY. The BODY stays @Damaged (Phase 2) for the entire episode — no patchwork, no gold-filled cracks, no bioluminescent core, no new parts. The VISIBLE reconstruction described above begins in EP09. EP08's single visible inner-change marker is the climax eyes steadying from glitch to calm blue (not a body change). Two-beat arc: EP08 strips bare / frees the awareness; EP09 mends the body with gold.

mentor.name: The Cosmic Mentor
mentor.archetype: The Wise Old Man (Jung) / The Sage / The Dusk-Born Psychiatrist
mentor.base_visual_prompt: Figure in a dark green cloak, leather tunic, deep wisdom, organic texture, holding a wooden staff with glowing raw amber tip. Contrast with Robotiko: Warm/Organic vs. Cold/Chrome. He exists between worlds — neither fully in light nor in darkness.
mentor.key_characteristic: He is not a superior — he is a fellow traveler who has already walked the wasteland. He speaks from experience, not authority. His amber staff tip glows warm gold, always contrasting with Robotiko's cold chrome.

status_notes.ep07: The Mentor does not die dramatically. He simply is no longer there. His absence is the final lesson. Robotiko must walk the last stretch alone.
status_notes.ep08_10: The Mentor may appear in memory fragments, flashbacks, or as an echo — but never as a physical presence.

robochica.name: Robochica
robochica.role: Robotiko's first encounter with love. Triggers emotional overclocking. She is not a villain — she is a mirror. What Robotiko projects onto her reveals more about him than about her.
robochica.base_visual_prompt: Retro-futuristic chrome female android, 70s sci-fi feminine form — elegant curves in chrome plating, distinct from Robotiko but clearly from the same aesthetic universe. Exposed warm-toned analog wires (gold and copper), glowing amber-gold eyes (steady, warm), subtle scratches and minor wear marks on chrome (NOT pristine, carries her own history). Art deco-influenced head shape, slightly more elongated than Robotiko. One unique visual signature: a fractal/mandala pattern etched into her left shoulder plate, identifiable even in silhouette.
robochica.eye_color: amber-gold (steady, warm — carries the color of TRUTH from EP04's amber DNA, creating structural irony: Robotiko unconsciously sees the Mentor's teaching in her eyes)
robochica.wire_colors: gold and copper (warm tones, contrasting Robotiko's blue and red)
robochica.visual_signature: Fractal/mandala pattern etched into left shoulder plate — identifiable even in partial views or silhouette
robochica.damage_level: Subtle — minor scratches, slight wear marks. Significantly cleaner than Robotiko's Phase 2 damage but NOT pristine. She has her own history, her own journey.

dramaturgy_rules.mirror_principle: She is a mirror — reveals more about Robotiko than about herself. Her body language is always ambiguous: could be receptive or indifferent. The audience fills in what they want, just as Robotiko does.
dramaturgy_rules.face_visibility: Maximum 3 clear face-on shots per episode. All other scenes: partial view, profile, silhouette, reflection in Robotiko's chrome, or obscured by light/shadow.
dramaturgy_rules.no_clear_emotions: Never show Robochica expressing clear, unambiguous emotions. She is what Robotiko projects onto her.
dramaturgy_rules.not_a_villain: She does nothing wrong. The tragedy is Robotiko's projection, not her actions.
